flagged.title: The >70% rule and the -250 floor overlap only between 70.00% and 71.43%
flagged.detail: A zero-vig fair price of -250 is exactly 1.400 decimal, or 71.4286%. Any selection above that probability prices shorter than -250 and fails the requested window; any selection at or below 70.00% fails the probability rule. The desk therefore treats the window as the binding constraint and publishes bigger favourites as Medium with the exclusion reason stated. A 5% bookmaker margin makes the overlap disappear entirely on offered prices, so the band test uses the zero-vig fair price and the offered price is shown separately.

flagged.title: Carried evidence is capped at Medium even when it lands inside the band
flagged.detail: 4 rows have carried official inputs and an in-band 70-71.43% selection (darts 2, rugby-league 2). They keep their prices but cannot be High, because this desk did not re-read the source; every one is published as Medium with the cap stated on the row.

flagged.title: The model is transparent but not calibrated out of sample
flagged.detail: Every price comes from a documented logit or normal model with published constants. There is no measured hit rate for these constants and no closing-line value study. A High label means the desk's stated rule was satisfied, not that a 71% winner has been demonstrated.
flagged.source: Methodology page; model constants in data/fec05fb4/desk.json method

flagged.detail: Tennis (11), snooker (11), cricket (5), golf (4) and eSports (1) rows carry a date but no verified clock. They are published blank and unpriced on their category pages and are not counted as upcoming.

flagged.title: The NHL record-only model disagrees with the market reference
flagged.detail: NHL.com publishes a DraftKings moneyline beside every game. The model, which uses only points percentage, differs by up to 21 points from the de-vigged market on this board. No NHL row can be High while that gap exists, and the size of the gap is printed on every NHL row.

flagged.title: MLB postseason records are 0-0 in the official payload
flagged.detail: The World Series schedule reports leagueRecord 0-0 for both clubs, so the model uses the final regular-season records (Brewers 103-59, Rays 98-64). Pitchers, bullpens, parks and postseason effects are not modelled, and all five games share the same two inputs.

flagged.title: Five categories have no verified upcoming fixture
flagged.detail: Tennis, snooker, golf, greyhounds and eSports have no row with a verified future start time at this cut-off. Their pages show the captured listings, blank and flagged, rather than invented fixtures. This is a coverage gap, not a claim that no such fixtures exist.

flagged.title: EuroLeague evidence expires at tip-off
flagged.detail: The nine EuroLeague rows tip off between 17:30Z on 22 October and 18:45Z on 23 October. This desk is an as-of 12:45Z snapshot; after those times the rows are historical and must not be read as pre-match picks.

flagged.title: OLBG is discovery only, never evidence
flagged.detail: OLBG cards were used to find events and to see what the market discusses. They set no rating, price or confidence, and no OLBG number is copied into this dataset.

flagged.title: Desk-defined Medium and Low thresholds
flagged.detail: Medium = an in-band 70-71.43% selection that fails the High evidence test, or a winner at 62%+. Low = anything else that is priced. These thresholds are the desk's own; they are not industry standards.

flagged.title: 2 High selections, 37 Medium and 48 Low/unpriced
flagged.detail: Both Highs are EuroLeague handicap or total lines originated at a 70-71.43% cover, not moneylines. Each carries a unique 60-word prediction, two-sided official evidence and a fresh read of the availability report. No High was issued for a big favourite just because it was a big favourite.

analysis.lede: This desk re-derives every non-excluded sport on the OLBG board from official sources and originates its own prices. It publishes two High selections, not because two is a target, but because the three gates — a 70-71.43% fair price, a fresh official read, and both clubs' availability confirmed — only coincide twice on 22-23 October 2026.

points.title: Why only two Highs
points.body: 87 upcoming fixtures carry a verified start time; 39 of them are priced inside the desk's rules. Every other in-band line belongs to a game where at least one club had not filed its Round 7 availability report, or to a sport whose official source could not be re-read this session.

points.title: The band is a knife-edge
points.body: Between 70.00% and 71.43% the fair price runs from -233 to -250. A stronger favourite cannot be priced inside the requested window at all; the desk publishes those as Medium rather than stretching the rule.

points.title: Where the desk is weakest
points.body: NHL prices come from points percentage alone and disagree with the published market by up to 21 points. MLB prices use regular-season records with no pitcher information. Darts, rugby league, rugby union, handball, volleyball, Australian rules and Gaelic football rely on evidence captured earlier in the day and are capped at Medium.
